summary: S&P 500 closed at 7,543.64 on Jul 9 (+0.81%), about 0.9% below the Jun 2 all-time high of 7,609.78, with chip stocks leading gains even as an Iran-related oil-price flare-up briefly rattled sentiment — the market has largely shrugged off that geopolitical scare. Breadth strengthened to roughly 70% of S&P 500 names above their 50-day moving average (vs ~67% on Jul 7), and the index sits comfortably above both its 50-day (~7,403) and 200-day (~6,948) averages, a genuinely healthy technical picture. VIX is 16.90, up 4.8% on the day but still in contango (VIX3M above spot) — elevated chop, not panic. The near-term calendar is light until June CPI on Jul 14, then a real event cluster forms: GOOGL earnings Jul 22, then FOMC (Jul 28–29) colliding with MSFT/META/AAPL earnings and June PCE (Jul 30) in the same week. The Fed remains on hold at 3.50–3.75% with a hawkish June dot plot and core PCE still running ~3.4% YoY, so a hot CPI or hawkish FOMC surprise is the real risk to this otherwise constructive setup. New cash: small selective entries are reasonable now through Jul 13, then pause into the CPI print and reassess.
